extraction.name: SQuAD: 100,000+ Questions for Machine Comprehension of Text
extraction.description: We present the Stanford Question Answering Dataset (SQuAD), a new reading comprehension dataset consisting of 100,000+ questions posed by crowdworkers on a set of Wikipedia articles, where the answer to each question is a segment of text from the corresponding reading passage.
extraction.creator: Pranav Rajpurkar and Jian Zhang and Konstantin Lopyrev and Percy Liang
extraction.rai:dataCollection: We collect our dataset in three stages: curating passages, crowdsourcing question-answers on those passages, and obtaining additional answers.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: To retrieve high-quality articles, we used Project Nayuki’s Wikipedia’s internal PageRanks to obtain the top 10000 articles of English Wikipedia, from which we sampled 536 articles uniformly at random. From each of these articles, we extracted individual paragraphs, stripping away images, figures, tables, and discarding paragraphs shorter than 500 characters.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: We partitioned the articles randomly into a training set (80%), a development set (10%), and a test set (10%).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: On each paragraph, crowdworkers were tasked with asking and answering up to 5 questions on the content of that paragraph. The questions had to be entered in a text field, and the answers had to be highlighted in the paragraph. To get an indication of human performance on SQuAD and to make our evaluation more robust, we obtained at least 2 additional answers for each question in the development and test sets.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Daemo platform (Gaikwad et al., 2015), with Amazon Mechanical Turk as its backend.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Over the development and test sets, 2.6% of questions were marked unanswerable by at least one of the additional crowdworkers.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: At least 3 answers per question in the development and test sets (1 original + 2 additional).
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Crowdworkers were required to have a 97% HIT acceptance rate, a minimum of 1000 HITs, and be located in the United States or Canada.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The span constraint also comes with the important benefit that span-based answers are easier to evaluate than free-form answers.
